cards.headline: White takes first and threatens at once; Black needs one approach and two threats more: S[A-1KO-] by your answer to question 1b, not S[A+1KO-].

diagrams.caption: The tree's line to the leaf marked S[A+1KO-], White to play. White can take the ko at a by capturing Black 5. The second ko is at b, where Black can capture White 2; c is Black's approach point.
White 6 takes the ko. If Black plays elsewhere, White 8 captures the stone at B18 and lives, even when Black holds four threats. White's capture needs no approach.

diagrams.moves: B19 A19! C18 A17 E19 B19 A18 pass D19
diagrams.caption: One threat more is not enough. Black 7 retakes after a threat, and Black 9 takes the second ko. White 10 takes E19, Black's approach point, and White 12 retakes the second ko without a threat. Black has none left, and White 14 captures four stones. Black's other answers to White 8 and White 10 fail too.

diagrams.moves: B19 A19! pass A17 G18 E19 A18 F17 B19 A19! C18 A17 pass D19
diagrams.caption: With two threats more Black kills. Black 9 takes the second ko before Black 11 approaches at E19: once White has played elsewhere at move 8, this order wins in both search areas, while approaching first fails in the wider one. Black 15 retakes after the second threat, Black 17 takes the second ko again, and Black 19 captures White's group.

text: S[A+1KO-] says White needs an approach and that Black wins at equal threats. Both are wrong, in both search areas. White 6 takes first and threatens at once (Diagram 2). Black fails even with one threat more than White (Diagram 3); with two, Black kills (Diagram 4). The count of two is proven only in the checker's narrow search area; in the wider area, where White has extra moves against Black's stone at F18, three is not ruled out.

In Diagram 4, Black 7 retakes but threatens nothing yet: White plays elsewhere at move 8 for free. Black needs one approach, Black 11 at E19, before its capture at A17 in the second ko threatens to kill. Black 11 captures nothing, so White 12 retakes the second ko for free, and Black 17 must capture there again.

You answered question 1b on 16 November: after Black's one approach the ko switches there and back through the second ko, each side then needing a capture and one more move, and you rate such a symmetric ko as a normal ko. So this is your one-move approach ko for Black: S[A-1KO-]. The checker counted Black's capture at A17 as a second approach (S[A-2KO+], the same threats); by your answer it is none.
No move's grade changes: any ko beats the ALIVE and SEKI leaves. Only the problem's status, taken from its best leaf, changes from S[A+1KO-] to S[A-1KO-].
